title: Physiological extrauterine support through fetal organ maturity

concept.text: The innovation would provide extremely premature infants with a temporary continuation of fetal physiology outside the uterus, allowing immature organs to develop before the infant begins air breathing. In the proposed pumpless approach, blood passes through an external gas-exchange circuit connected to the umbilical vessels, driven by the fetal heart. A closed fluid environment keeps the lungs fluid-filled while the circuit performs gas exchange. The intended capability is sustained physiological support through a meaningful period of organ maturation, followed by a safe transition to neonatal life.

This is partial continuation of gestational physiology after premature delivery, rather than reproduction of an entire pregnancy. It combines neonatal and fetal medicine with obstetrics, cardiovascular physiology, extracorporeal engineering, nutrition, and developmental neuroscience. Supporting human growth and maturation comparable to development in utero remains a performance goal; the supplied animal evidence does not establish that outcome in humans.

significance.text: Extremely premature infants must begin pulmonary gas exchange while their lungs and other organs remain immature. Respiratory support and other intensive-care interventions can contribute to injury during this vulnerable period. A successful extrauterine system would change the timing of that transition: it would delay exposure of immature lungs to gas ventilation while supporting continued development. Preserving fluid-filled lungs and the physiological conditions needed for lung growth provides a concrete biological basis for this approach.

If comparative human studies showed better survival and less severe chronic lung disease or brain injury, the approach could fundamentally change care at the edge of viability. Those benefits do not follow automatically from delaying ventilation. Extrauterine support cannot be assumed to prevent pre-existing injury, all complications of prematurity, or injury introduced by the circuit and transfer procedure. In particular, reassuring observations in lamb brains do not establish protection against human germinal-matrix or intraventricular hemorrhage.

Synthesis: describing the system as a continuation of gestation captures its intended physiological bridge, but should not imply that it replaces every maternal and placental function or guarantees normal development. Deployment in hospitals without neonatal intensive-care capability would require additional advances in reliability, staffing, infrastructure, and transfer arrangements. Development outside the mother beginning at conception would require a substantially broader capability than this innovation.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing clinical capability is days to weeks of stable umbilical support in a fluid environment that preserves fetal circulation, supports human organ growth and maturation, and permits a safe transition to air breathing. The engineering challenge is simultaneous: umbilical access must remain functional, circuit resistance and flow must suit the fetal circulation, and the fetal heart must drive adequate gas exchange without harmful loading. Vascular spasm, contamination, and nutritional management are interdependent barriers rather than separate problems that can be solved in isolation.

A human target window around 22–24 weeks should be treated as a proposed clinical scope, not a demonstrated developmental equivalence. The 2017 investigators discussed an initial population of approximately 23–25 weeks. Their lamb model principally approximated human pulmonary maturity; younger lambs were needed to study more relevant stages of brain development. No single animal-to-human gestational conversion establishes equivalent maturity across lungs, brain, and the rest of the body.

Translation also requires reliable transfer from placental support to the external circuit and, later, from extrauterine support to neonatal care. Transfer may require planned surgical delivery, introducing maternal risks and limiting which circumstances are technically suitable. Human circulatory responses, neurological safety, and long-term developmental benefit remain unresolved in the supplied evidence. These clinical boundaries must be established alongside circuit performance.

current_state.text: In 2017, Partridge, Davey, Flake, and colleagues reported physiological support of fetal lambs for up to four weeks in Nature Communications, doi:10.1038/ncomms15112. Reported achievements included stable gas exchange and circulation, somatic growth, lung maturation, and measured brain growth and myelination. These results establish a substantial animal technical basis. Human developmental equivalence was principally pulmonary, and the authors qualified the neurological interpretation; the findings do not establish multi-week support or normal development in human infants.

In June 2024, Peers de Nieuwburgh and colleagues reported results in less mature lambs in Pediatric Research, doi:10.1038/s41390-024-03287-0. Ten included lambs received support for a mean of 13.5 days, with a range of 10–21 days. Four additional lambs died before the study endpoint and were excluded. The duration and developmental findings therefore need to be read with the exclusions in view; they do not describe successful completion in every animal entering the experiment.

Brain MRI and histology in that 2024 study were assessed in six supported lambs. Maturation was qualitatively comparable to controls, and no white-matter injury or germinal-matrix/intraventricular hemorrhage was observed in the assessed sample. However, brains were smaller than those of age-matched controls, and the study was underpowered to detect even major developmental differences. The authors explicitly stated that this extremely preterm lamb model does not predict human hemorrhage risk. These observations are useful evidence about the examined animals, but do not establish neurological equivalence or human brain safety.

A BCNatal institutional announcement dated 3 July 2026 reported 21 days of support in a sheep model and a planned first human trial in 2028–2029, dependent on preparation and investment. This is an institutional report of animal work and a prospective timetable, not a peer-reviewed human outcome. The supplied review also notes that the announcement page flags automatic translation.

A Baker Institute policy report dated 21 July 2026 described mixed animal safety and efficacy findings, significant remaining technical revisions, and anticipated first-in-human trials within the following decade. It called for further guidance for such trials within existing device regulation; this should not be interpreted as an absence of regulatory authority. Its broad forecast and BCNatal's project-specific timetable are projections with different scopes, rather than conflicting demonstrated outcomes.

Evidence boundary: the supplied sources document no human outcome, and the July 2026 policy report described the technology as untested in humans at that time. No bounded literature-search record was supplied to establish whether peer-reviewed human reports existed by 1 November 2026. The supplied review covered the complete main text of the 2017 article and all ten pages of the 2024 article, but did not inspect linked supplements or figure images. The source index reports no extraction truncation or extraction issues; those facts do not extend the review to uninspected material or establish exhaustive literature coverage.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed feasibility demonstration: a prospective first-in-human series would enroll infants who would otherwise receive intensive care, using prespecified gestational-age bounds, clinical eligibility, and technical transfer requirements. It would demonstrate successful umbilical connection, sustained fetal physiology for a clinically meaningful interval, growth toward a prespecified maturity endpoint, and transition to air breathing and neonatal care. Maternal outcomes and failed transfers would be included in the assessment. These are proposed criteria, not established regulatory standards.
completion_criteria.label: Human fetal support sustains maturation through transition to air breathing

completion_criteria.text: Proposed efficacy demonstration: subsequent adequately powered comparative studies would assess survival and freedom from severe chronic lung disease and severe brain injury. A small first-in-human series could establish feasibility but would not alone establish comparative benefit. Contemporaneous controls would require attention to prognostic factors beyond gestational age, differences in treatment eligibility, and selection bias. Reporting would account for every attempted transfer, early death, exclusion, and incomplete follow-up so that developmental findings are not interpreted only among successful completers.
completion_criteria.label: Comparisons assess survival without severe chronic lung disease or brain injury

completion_criteria.text: Proposed field-level demonstration: more than one center would reproduce sustained support and safe transition, with follow-up into childhood to assess neurodevelopment and other consequential morbidity. Studies would define practical limits, including gestational and clinical eligibility, achievable support duration, maternal delivery requirements, complications, and the expertise and infrastructure needed. Finite demonstrations would establish performance across the populations and circumstances tested; they would not establish universal suitability or development identical to that in utero.
completion_criteria.label: Centers reproduce sustained support and safe transition with childhood follow-up

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PED-05, Prevention of cerebral palsy after perinatal brain injury, has the closest neurological overlap. PED-01 aims to support development during extreme prematurity and might reduce some exposures that contribute to injury; PED-05 concerns preventing cerebral palsy after an injury has occurred. Neither outcome establishes the other. PED-04, Controlled reopening of developmental critical periods, and PED-09, Post-symptomatic restoration of severe genetic neurodevelopmental disorders, concern changing developmental capacity or function after a developmental trajectory has already been altered, whereas PED-01 aims to sustain maturation during an early vulnerable period.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-06, Prenatal correction that lets severe monogenic disease develop normally, and PED-11, One-time in vivo correction of severe newborn metabolic disease before irreversible injury, share the importance of intervention before lasting developmental damage. Their defining capability is correction of a disease cause. PED-01 supplies a physiological environment for continued maturation and would not itself correct a pathogenic variant or metabolic defect.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-07, A physiological subpulmonary ventricle for single-ventricle heart disease, overlaps in cardiovascular engineering and the need to match support to circulatory physiology. Its objective is a physiological subpulmonary pumping function for a congenital cardiac condition. PED-01 instead depends on preserving fetal circulation while the fetal heart drives an external gas-exchange circuit. PED-08, Restoration of nephron endowment after the nephrogenic clock stops, concerns restoration after a developmental production window has closed; PED-01 concerns support during ongoing development and does not establish the ability to restart nephron formation.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-03, Reversal of established childhood stunting and its cognitive cost, shares an interest in growth and developmental outcomes but addresses reversal of established deficits later in childhood. Growth during extrauterine fetal support would not demonstrate reversal of stunting or recovery of its cognitive consequences. PED-02, Protective adaptive immunity generated by the newborn, concerns the newborn's own immune capability; keeping an extrauterine circuit sterile is a support requirement, not evidence of that immune breakthrough.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-12, Drug-free donor-specific tolerance for pediatric solid-organ grafts, and PED-13, Drug-free reset of severe pediatric autoimmune disease, concern durable changes in immune specificity or regulation. They remain distinct from temporary support of fetal physiology. PED-10, Function-sparing cure of H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma, shares the goal of preserving neurological function in children, but its defining challenge is curing a malignancy while sparing function, rather than sustaining organ maturation after premature delivery.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether peer-reviewed human outcomes existed by 1 November 2026; no bounded freshness search was provided.
Safe human eligibility, transfer procedures, support duration, maturity endpoints, and maternal delivery requirements remain to be established.
Human circulatory responses, hemorrhage risk, comparative survival and morbidity, and childhood developmental outcomes remain undemonstrated in this evidence set.
The 2024 study's exclusions, small brain-analysis sample, smaller brains, and limited power leave uncertainty about developmental equivalence and neurological safety.
The supplied review did not inspect the animal papers' supplements or figure images; this record does not infer additional findings from those materials.
BCNatal's 2028–2029 trial plan remains conditional on preparation and investment; neither supplied forecast establishes when human trials will occur.

brief.title: More time for premature babies’ organs to mature
possible: Babies born far too early could have more time for their organs to develop before they begin breathing air. A fluid-filled enclosure would keep their lungs filled with liquid, while their own heart drives blood through an external device that exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide through the umbilical cord.
why: Extremely premature babies must use lungs that are still developing. Breathing support can injure those fragile lungs. Delaying air breathing could let them mature under conditions closer to those in the womb.
For these babies and their families, the hoped-for change is better survival with less severe lasting lung disease or brain injury.

sources.who: Emily A Partridge, Marcus G Davey, Alan W Flake and colleagues
sources.showed: They supported premature lambs for up to four weeks, maintaining circulation and oxygen exchange while their bodies, lungs and brains developed.
sources.quote: Lambs on support maintain stable haemodynamics, have normal blood gas and oxygenation parameters and maintain patency of the fetal circulation.
sources.cited_for: The system can sustain development outside the womb in premature lambs.
sources.not_established: The lambs mainly matched human lung maturity; their development does not establish human brain safety or successful human support.

sources.who: Maureen Peers de Nieuwburgh and colleagues
sources.showed: Less mature lambs maintained stable circulation and oxygen levels and continued growing. Four lambs died early and were excluded from the study results.
sources.quote: Animals showed growth and physiologic cardiac function.
sources.cited_for: Support is possible in less mature lambs, whose brains better approximate the intended human developmental stage.
sources.not_established: The small brain study cannot establish normal brain development or predict human brain bleeding risk.

sources.showed: The team reported supporting sheep for 21 days in a liquid incubator and successfully transferring lambs to life outside it. This was an institutional announcement.
sources.quote: The project has carried out trials that have resulted in viable lambs following their time in the liquid incubator.
sources.cited_for: Another team reported sustained animal support followed by a successful transition to air breathing.
sources.not_established: Animal survival and transition do not establish safe use or developmental benefit in human babies.

sources.who: Janeilya Davis and colleagues, Rice University’s Baker Institute
sources.showed: They reviewed animal research and the clinical, ethical and regulatory questions surrounding initial human trials, identifying technical problems that still need work.
sources.cited_for: Moving from animal experiments to human trials requires further technical development and clear trial safeguards.
sources.not_established: A policy review does not demonstrate safety, effectiveness or readiness for human treatment.

shown: Partridge, Davey, Flake and colleagues supported premature lambs for up to four weeks while their organs developed. Some lambs subsequently transitioned to life outside the system.

The same research programme sustained less mature lambs, but early deaths were excluded from its results. Brain examinations found no observed injury in a small sample, yet the brains were smaller than those of comparable lambs developing in the womb.
missing: Human babies would need sustained support that preserves circulation, permits organ maturation and ends in a safe transition to air breathing.
Transfer procedures would need to work reliably, with acceptable risks for both baby and mother.
Comparative studies would need to establish better survival and fewer severe lung and brain injuries.
Follow-up would need to establish childhood development and lasting health outcomes.

milestones.label: Human babies mature on support and begin air breathing
milestones.explanation: An initial human series would have to demonstrate sustained support, maturation and transition, while accounting for failed transfers and maternal outcomes. This would establish feasibility.

milestones.label: Comparisons show survival without severe lung disease or brain injury
milestones.explanation: Adequately sized comparative studies would have to assess survival without severe lung disease or brain injury, accounting for all attempted transfers and losses. This would establish whether babies benefit.

milestones.label: Several centres repeat success with childhood follow-up
milestones.explanation: Several centres would have to reproduce sustained support and safe transition, track childhood outcomes and define practical limits. This would establish how reliably the approach works across tested settings.

uncertain: It remains unclear which babies could safely receive support, how long they should remain on it and what maturity should trigger transition.
Lamb brain findings cannot settle human brain bleeding risk or whether development would match development in the womb.
The effects of the external blood circuit on human circulation, and the delivery risks for mothers, remain unresolved.

page.title: Artificial womb support for extremely premature infants
page.definition: An infant born before 28 completed weeks of gestation continues organ development outside the uterus while a fluid-filled enclosure keeps the lungs liquid-filled and an umbilical blood circuit exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide. Support preserves fetal circulation and ends with transition to air breathing and neonatal care.

goal.need: An estimated 567,800 infants were born before 28 weeks worldwide in 2020. At 19 US academic centers in 2013–2018, 30.0% of infants actively treated at birth at 22 weeks and 55.8% at 23 weeks survived to discharge or to one year if still hospitalized. Ventilation can injure immature lungs faster than they can grow and repair. Delaying lung ventilation could give more infants time to mature and survive with fewer lasting complications, provided those gains outweigh risks such as bleeding and clotting in the blood circuit.

figures.caption: Survival to discharge or one year among infants actively treated at birth.
figures.note: These are outcomes under neonatal care in the registry cohort, not artificial womb outcomes.

completion.title: FDA approves an artificial womb system for continued maturation of extremely premature infants.
completion.criterion: FDA grants premarket approval (PMA) to a complete artificial womb system for supporting extremely premature infants in fetal physiology through further organ maturation and transition to neonatal care. Approval covers that intended use, population and conditions of use, on valid scientific evidence providing reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Premarket Approval framework under 21 CFR Part 814; FDA identifies artificial womb devices as Class III in its Pediatric Advisory Committee meeting of 19 September 2023.
completion.threshold_quote: sufficient valid scientific evidence to assure that the device is safe and effective for its intended use(s).
completion.basis: FDA classifies artificial womb devices as Class III, requiring premarket approval. This supplies an external test for clinical use despite the absence of an agreed numerical maturity endpoint. Vitara labels EXTEND investigational and states that its technology has no marketing authorization.

milestones.title: An artificial womb circuit sustains organ perfusion and oxygenation in a preterm animal.
milestones.criterion: In a preterm animal, the artificial womb circuit sustains blood flow sufficient to perfuse and oxygenate the organs.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, briefing for the Pediatric Advisory Committee on 19 September 2023, §3.3.1; these are published development considerations rather than finalized AWT guidance.
milestones.threshold_quote: maintain adequate extracorporeal circuit flow to support end organ perfusion and oxygenation.

milestones.title: Artificial womb support produces age-appropriate animal organ growth with protection from injury.
milestones.criterion: Animal studies show growth and maturation appropriate to gestational age and protection from injury across organ systems. Lung tissue progresses from the canalicular to the saccular stage, with better lung growth and development than in mechanically ventilated controls. Brain assessment covers regional growth, cortical and microstructural maturation, and injury in a developmentally relevant model. Assessment also covers the heart, kidneys, liver, skin and gastrointestinal tract.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, briefing for the Pediatric Advisory Committee on 19 September 2023, §3.3.1; organ maturation and injury protection are qualitative criteria without a fixed support duration.
milestones.threshold_quote: Normal growth and protection from injury should be demonstrated across organ systems

milestones.title: An artificial womb functions in an infant in an authorized first-in-human study.
milestones.criterion: In a US first-in-human study with FDA investigational device exemption and institutional review board approval, the complete system provides its intended support to an extremely premature infant. The study documents whether the device functions as intended, how the infant tolerates the procedures and any device-related complications.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, general early feasibility guidance, §3, and the AWT regulatory discussion on 19 September 2023; no AWT-specific numerical clinical success threshold is specified.
milestones.threshold_quote: initial clinical safety and device functionality

milestones.title: A pivotal human study establishes an artificial womb's safety and effectiveness for its intended use.
milestones.criterion: A pivotal human study provides definitive evidence of artificial womb safety and effectiveness for its specified intended use, using a statistically justified sample and meeting prospectively defined success criteria under a prespecified analysis plan. Under FDA's safety and effectiveness framework, probable health benefits outweigh probable risks and clinically significant results occur in a significant portion of the target population. Numerical endpoints and follow-up duration must be specified for the device and indication.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, general early feasibility guidance, §§3 and 5, and the safety and effectiveness framework in 21 CFR §860.7; these are general device criteria, not published AWT-specific numerical endpoints.
milestones.threshold_quote: definitive evidence of the safety and effectiveness of a device for a specified intended use

milestones.title: Animal studies evaluate adverse events attributable to the artificial womb.
milestones.criterion: Animal studies assess adverse events and their relationship to the device and its procedures. Assessments address the effects of the blood circuit on the developing heart, bleeding and thrombosis, and the ability to detect and treat infection.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Pediatric Advisory Committee discussion of animal safety endpoints, 19 September 2023, and FDA briefing §3.3.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: adverse events, especially those that could be attributed to the device, should be evaluated in animal studies

milestones.title: A preterm animal survives transfer from the artificial womb to gas exchange through its lungs.
milestones.criterion: After a period of artificial womb support, the animal leaves the fluid enclosure, is disconnected from the oxygenator and maintains gas exchange through its lungs. Mechanical ventilation may assist the transition.
milestones.set_by: Neonatal transition as evaluated in the EXTEND and BCNatal sheep studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: it moves from the liquid incubator to extrauterine life and begins to use its lungs like any newborn.

not_found: No published AWT-specific minimum support duration, maturity threshold for withdrawal or numerical clinical success criteria were found in FDA materials, developer pages or the supplied reports.

No public artificial womb first-in-human protocol or peer-reviewed human outcomes were found in web and ClinicalTrials.gov-indexed searches for artificial womb, artificial placenta and EXTEND through 14 November 2026.

results.finding: Eight preterm lambs maintained placental-range circuit flow and normal fetal oxygen delivery for up to 28 days.
results.detail: Five lambs began support at 105–108 days' gestation and three at 115–120 days. The longest runs ended at the animal protocol limit.
results.quote: We have run 8 lambs with maintenance of stable levels of circuit flow equivalent to the normal flow to the placenta.

results.finding: None of the five supported preterm lambs examined by whole-brain sectioning showed hemorrhage or infarct.
results.detail: The lung morphometry comparator was normal age-matched lambs. Near-term lambs ventilated after delivery served as pulmonary function controls. Wool growth and swallowing were observed without systematic skin or gastrointestinal maturation and injury assessments.
results.quote:
On whole-brain sectioning we observed no evidence of haemorrhage or infarct in any of the UA/UV animal brains (
n
=5).

results.finding: One of five preterm pilot lambs survived long-term after weaning to spontaneous breathing following 288 hours of support.
results.detail: The long-term survivor came from the semi-closed pilot using carotid artery and jugular vein access.
results.quote: Importantly, one animal was maintained on the circuit for 288 h (120–132 days of gestation) and was successfully weaned to spontaneous respiration, with long-term survival confirming that animals can be transitioned to normal postnatal life after prolonged extra-uterine support.

results.finding: Sepsis limited three of five preterm lamb runs in the semi-closed fluid-bath pilot.
results.detail: The closed Biobag series reported no clinically significant infections. The authors identify earlier ovine germinal matrix maturation as a limitation for assessing intracranial hemorrhage risk.
results.quote: However, sepsis remained limiting in 3 of 5 lambs resulting in design of a closed fluid circuit (the Biobag).

results.finding: EXTEND sustained physiologic perfusion and oxygenation in 10 extremely preterm lambs for up to 21 days.
results.detail: Four additional lambs died before the study endpoint and were excluded from the physiologic analysis.
results.quote:
The lambs demonstrate normal oxygen delivery
and metabolism with controlled circuit ﬂows for up to 21 days.

results.finding: Among 10 extremely preterm EXTEND lambs, the 6 assessed by brain MRI and histology showed maturation without ischemic or white matter injury.
results.detail: The authors considered the brain comparisons underpowered even for major differences. Several maturation measures were qualitative.
results.quote:
Notably, no ischemic or white matter injury was seen in
any of the experimental animals.

results.finding: Six of 10 extremely preterm EXTEND lambs required transfusion after blood loss from sampling and umbilical cord bleeding.
results.detail: The suspected air embolism and the proposed link between cord stretching and venous spasm were inferred from the circumstances.
results.quote:
Six lambs in the extremely preterm group needed
at least one transfusion of adult blood due cumulative blood loss
from blood sampling and umbilical cord bleeds while on EXTEND
(Table 2).

results.finding: Fetal sheep on the umbilical oxygenation circuit survived 21 days in good condition. Sample size unstated.
results.detail: The verdict uses sustained survival as functional evidence of adequate perfusion and oxygenation.
results.quote: which has achieved 21 days of survival in good condition in an experimental sheep model.

results.finding: One sheep had normal reported neurodevelopment after liquid incubator support and was over 1 year old at reporting.
results.quote:

results.finding: At least one lamb survived more than 13 months after transition from the liquid incubator. Total cohort size unstated.
results.detail: The article gives no oxygenator disconnection timing or ventilation details.
results.quote: Postnatal survival of more than 13 months has also been achieved, with good neurodevelopmental outcomes following treatment in the liquid incubator.

results.finding: Sheep transferred from the uterus into the prototype had zero reported incidents during transfer. Sample size unstated.
results.quote: Using a sheep model, the team has so far designed and described the surgical techniques and protocols required to carry out a transition from the uterus to a prototype liquid incubator without incident, and has achieved a survival rate of 21 days within the system.

results.finding: Twelve preterm lambs on EXTEND maintained physiologic oxygenation and hemodynamics for more than 14 days.
results.detail: Fifteen of 27 enrolled lambs died before the 14-day endpoint and were excluded from the physiologic analysis.
results.quote: Both study groups demonstrated overall hemodynamic stability, with no significant differences in blood flow or blood flow per weight.

results.finding: Twelve preterm lambs showed normal somatic growth during more than 14 days of EXTEND support.
results.detail: The study focused on oxygenator performance and hemocompatibility. It did not assess tissue-level effects or microthrombi.
results.quote: All animals demonstrated normal somatic growth.

results.finding: Among 12 preterm lambs completing EXTEND support, 11 required blood transfusion.
results.detail: Blood sampling and prematurity contributed to transfusion need alongside acute bleeding. The lamb with diminished right heart function also had an enclosure-fluid infection, leaving the contribution of oxygenator clotting uncertain.
results.quote: Eleven out of twelve animals (five in the heparin study and six in the heparin-free study) required transfusion, with mean volumes of 58.4 ± 21.6 and 50.0 ± 10.9 ml, respectively.

results.finding: Five preterm lambs received EXTEND support for up to 22 days.
results.detail: Table 1 gives the individual support durations, including a death from sepsis at day 16.
results.quote:
Lambs were maintained 
on EXTEND for up to 22 days, with studies terminated before this end-point if circuit flows or physiological 
parameters were considered incompatible with survival47.

results.finding: Among nine lambs, EXTEND brains differed from age-matched late preterm controls in expression of 331 genes.
results.detail: Neither control group showed histologic injury, so the comparison does not establish protection from injury.
results.quote: only 331 differentially expressed genes were found in the Late Pre-term control group.

results.finding: Among five EXTEND lambs, two died following sepsis or a cord bleed followed by a transfusion reaction.
results.detail: The events are documented in Table 1 footnotes.

results.finding: Preterm lambs supported on EXTEND (n=17) showed broadly age-appropriate ileal maturation after 14–28 days.
results.detail: Intestinal immune maturation was impaired despite preserved epithelial and enteric nervous system development.
results.quote: EXTEND supports normal ileal epithelial and enteric nervous system maturation in pre-term lambs.

results.finding: Preterm EXTEND lambs were delivered, ventilated and subsequently bottle-fed. The number of survivors was unspecified.
results.detail: The report gives no numerical transition outcome or support duration for this subset.
results.quote: In the animals that were delivered, ventilated, and formula fed, via orogastric and then bottle feeding, we did not see evidence of bowel necrosis or features of immaturity upon final histologic evaluation.

results.finding: Preterm EXTEND lambs (n=4) had fewer ileal Peyer’s patches than in utero controls (n=6, P < .00001).
results.detail: The authors proposed missing factors in the synthetic fluid or absent maternal or placental contributions. The mechanism remains unresolved.
results.quote: We did, however, see arrest of lymphoid follicle aggregation within the bowel in lambs developing within the EXTEND system.

results.finding: Early premature lambs on artificial placenta support (n=3) had lower lung injury scores than ventilated controls (n=5), with p=0.02.
results.detail: Early ventilated lambs averaged 4±3 hours of support. Artificial placenta support averaged 163±9 hours across both age cohorts. The authors acknowledged that tracheal occlusion may have accelerated lung development.
results.quote: Total injury scores at 121d were 1.7±2.1 for AP vs. 5.5±1.6 for MV (p=0.02).

results.finding: Premature lambs on artificial placenta support had higher cerebral peduncle fractional anisotropy than late ventilated controls (n = 4 per group, p = 0.006).
results.detail: Supported lambs were assessed after 7 days. Late ventilation controls began ventilation at 127 days of gestation and were assessed after up to 48 hours.
results.quote: Compared to late MV brains, AP brains demonstrated significantly higher ADC (0.45 ± 0.08 vs. 0.27 ± 0.11, p = 0.02) and FA (0.61 ± 0.04 vs. 0.44 ± 0.05; p = 0.006) in the cerebral peduncles.

results.finding: Premature fetal sheep (n unreported) showed age-appropriate regional myelination after up to 28 days of EXTEND support.
results.detail: The 28 days is the maximum support duration. The supplied text gives no quantitative myelination result or injury rate.
results.quote: the degree of myelination was regionally appropriate and consistent with age matched controls.

results.finding: Extremely preterm ovine fetuses on artificial placenta support (n=6) had lower lung, liver, and kidney weights than in utero controls (n=8), including 19% lower mean lung weight.
results.detail: The 19% difference is calculated from Table 1 means. The abstract lists six controls, while the Methods and Table 1 list eight. Three supported fetuses developed edema, which the authors say likely masked reduced somatic growth.
results.quote:
Fetal lung, liver, and kidney weights and humerus length gain in the APT Group were less than those of the
in-utero
Control Group.

results.finding: Premature lambs on artificial placenta support had a mean jejunal crypt depth of 77.5 µm, comparable to late tissue controls (n=5 per group).
results.detail: Controls were sampled at delivery. The similar crypt depths are consistent with preserved architecture, but the small sample limits conclusions about maturation and injury. Epithelial injury and congestion were more frequent in the distal jejunum of supported lambs and did not meet the study’s significance threshold.
results.quote: Although the CD in AP bowel (77.5±5.9) was not statistically different than ETC (p=0.16) and LTC (p=0.99), there was an increasing trend of AP CD similar to that of the LTC group.

results.finding: In 7 fetal lambs on EXTEND, combined cardiac output fell to 482 mL/min/kg at the highest circuit resistance tested.
results.detail: The cardiac response was measured after short changes in circuit resistance. The authors reported stable qualitative ventricular function during testing and ruled out cardiac dysfunction and high-output heart failure as causes of the two later deaths.
results.quote: This decline continues, with a further reduction to 482 ± 48 mL/min/kg at State 3 ( p  = 0.028).

results.finding: Among 10 extremely premature lambs on artificial placenta support, lung histology found focal arterial thrombi or thromboemboli in 4 lambs on the nitric oxide circuit.
results.detail: The pulmonary clots were microscopic findings. Their clinical significance after artificial placenta support remained unknown because the lambs were euthanized without weaning. Antimicrobials were given prophylactically.
results.quote: No animals in the Heparin group had evidence of thrombosis, whereas four animals in the NOSA group had focal arterial thrombi or thromboemboli; these tended to be rare and were located in the periphery in all but one instance.

results.finding: In the longer-support cohort of fetal lambs on an artificial placenta (n = 10), 2 developed sepsis.
results.detail: The study used prophylactic antibiotics and reported sepsis without describing how it was diagnosed or whether treatment succeeded. The authors also identified limited suitability of this lamb model for assessing intracranial hemorrhage.
results.quote: Among the 48–168 h survival group, 4 out of 10 fetal lambs presented complications after the first day, consisting in cannulation accidents leading to interruption of flow (n = 2) and sepsis (n = 2).

results.finding: Among 10 extremely preterm sheep fetuses on artificial placenta support, 2 were euthanized after catheter obstruction caused circuit failure.
results.detail: The two fetuses with circuit failure were excluded from further analyses. The in-utero comparison could not isolate the effects of the blood circuit from surgery and other aspects of support.
results.quote: Two EVE animals died due to catheter-based circuit compromise.

goal.need = "An estimated 567,800 infants were born before 28 weeks worldwide in 2020. At 19 US academic centers in 2013\u20132018, 30.0% of infants actively treated at birth at 22 weeks and 55.8% at 23 weeks survived to discharge or to one year if still hospitalized. Ventilation can injure immature lungs faster than they can grow and repair. Delaying lung ventilation could give more infants time to mature and survive with fewer lasting complications, provided those gains outweigh risks such as bleeding and clotting in the blood circuit.". Reason: The current paragraph gives the registry size and points to missing figures without stating the survival rates or explaining why delaying lung ventilation could help.

add statement by Perinatal Life Support consortium, EU Horizon 2020 grant 863087, 2019: "support the safe development of EP infants outside the womb by preserving the innate fetal cardiorespiratory physiology ex vivo". Reason: The Horizon 2020 grant records an independent European consortium’s goal and identifies the proof of principle it was funded to deliver.

edit m1: criterion = "In a preterm animal, the artificial womb circuit sustains blood flow sufficient to perfuse and oxygenate the organs."; threshold_quote = "maintain adequate extracorporeal circuit flow to support end organ perfusion and oxygenation."; threshold_ref = 8; refs = [8]. Reason: The criterion mixes FDA’s functional test with flow rates and support durations observed in particular lamb studies.

edit m2: criterion = "Animal studies show growth and maturation appropriate to gestational age and protection from injury across organ systems. Lung tissue progresses from the canalicular to the saccular stage, with better lung growth and development than in mechanically ventilated controls. Brain assessment covers regional growth, cortical and microstructural maturation, and injury in a developmentally relevant model. Assessment also covers the heart, kidneys, liver, skin and gastrointestinal tract."; threshold_quote = "Normal growth and protection from injury should be demonstrated across organ systems"; threshold_ref = 8; refs = [8]. Reason: The current criterion devotes most of its text to one lamb study and leaves the scope of FDA’s multi-organ assessment unclear.

add milestone after m2: "Animal studies evaluate adverse events attributable to the artificial womb.". Reason: The animal milestones cover perfusion and growth but omit the FDA panel’s separate assessment of harms attributable to the device.

add milestone after m2: "A preterm animal survives transfer from the artificial womb to gas exchange through its lungs.". Reason: Lung maturation during support and successful gas exchange after disconnection are distinct results that the existing milestones cannot distinguish.
